searchText: state root mismatch Hot fix for blockchain tests is out: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/pectra-devnet-3%40v1.3.0 PTAL <@543900561460822016> <@758579010027782144> <@583892532644151312> <@827653956955406406> <@429719902363058177> <@508125616940515329> cc: <@348892132247076864> 🙂 One more release for today: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/pectra-devnet-3%40v1.4.0 Fixes expectation on some tests with invalid authorization list signatures. <@892053833121923094> quick question: aside from understanding python, what other prerequisites should a test writer have to effectively generate tests? Do you mean like generating the fixtures or writing the test cases? either; i want to understand what skillset is necessary to carry out an execution spec test from start to finish, and what a testwriter should expect in terms of time commitment, etc. I'd say that EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) knowledge is extremely important, and the time commitment really depends on the EIP, it could be one week for a [simple EIP](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5656), but some can take [months even](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7692). Take a look into the implemented tests here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/tree/main/tests they are categorized into forks and then EIPs, so you can get an idea of the complexity difference
